The type of services are the same as the services described in the performance work statement for the master IDIQ contract, 89303322DEM000084, and currently being performed on the current WVDP TAC Task Order, 89303323FEM400321 (hereinafter the �Current WVDP TAC Task Order�). The Site TACs IDIQ has a five (5) year ordering period, with a period of performance from September 20, 2022 to September 19, 2027. Under the chosen IDIQ contract type, the authority exists to issue logical follow-on task orders. The FAR and the Site TACs IDIQ (H.41 Task Ordering Procedure) provide statutory and contractual exceptions to the Fair Opportunity process. Among these exceptions is the issuance of a Task Order on a sole-source basis in the interest of economy and efficiency as a logical follow-on to an order already issued under the IDIQ contract, provided that all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be considered for the original WVDP Task Order. All eligible EM Site TACs contract holders were provided a fair opportunity to compete for this work. Before issuance of the current WVDP TAC Task Order, all seven holders of Site TACs contracts were provided a Request for Task Order Proposal on November 4, 2022 with a requested proposal submission deadline of November 20, 2022. Six (6) contractors submitted proposals in response to the solicitation and FPM AECOM JV1 was selected. Thus, contract provisions put all eligible Site TACs IDIQ contractors on notice at the time the Current WVDP TAC Task Order was solicited that DOE could issue the awardee a sole-source logical follow-on task order. description: INDUSTRY ANNOUNCEMENT: INTENT TO ISSUE CHALLENGE STATEMENT for the United States Space Command (USSPACECOM) Command and Control Facility (C2F): Design Build Contractor (DBC) Acquisition Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) seeks a partner to serve as the DBC responsible for the design, construction, fit out, commissioning, and accreditation of the USSPACECOM C2F. The selected contractor will be responsible for providing a mission-ready facility by December 2031. The DBC will be responsible for design and construction of the facility, including all associated Command, Control, Communication, and Computer Information Technology (C4IT) and Fixtures, Furniture and Equipment (FF&E), and must be skilled in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Additionally, the DBC will be responsible for providing Construction Surveillance Technicians to ensure construction meets ICD-705 standards in collaboration with the AFCEC team�s SSMs. This integrated, holistic approach is a significant departure from prior MILCON construction norms; our intent is to provide qualified design-builders time to establish expanded partnerships in advance of the Challenge Statement release. This mission critical facility, and its supporting data center, is required to support approximately 1,800 personnel and cost approximately $4B to design, build, fit-out, commission, accredit, install FF&E. The C2F will incorporate Radio Frequency (RF) shielding, High-Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP) protection, Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) / Special Access Program (SAP) construction, and redundant and resilient infrastructure.
